title: Lamborghini’s Temerario Spyder Boasts Company’s First Power-Folding Hardtop

body_markdown:
Lamborghinis and convertibles go together like wine and pasta, but the latest creation from the Sant’Agata automaker marks a new milestone for drop-top Lambos. Meet the Temerario Spyder, the first convertible Lamborghini to feature a powered retractable hardtop mechanism.


Lamborghini


Ten electronic actuators work in conjunction to pull the roof panel off, slide it back, and fold it away. It’s the first time a Lamborghini droptop uses an entirely electric system for the task; the company’s most recent droptop, the[Huracán EVO Spyder](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/lamborghini-drops-the-huracan-evo-rwds-top-with-the-new-610-hp-spyder/) , utilized an electrohydraulic system to store its soft top. Lamborghini says the new electronic system is both quieter and more compact.


Lamborghini


That compactness enables another impressive feat of engineering: When retracted, the hardtop folds vertically behind the cabin, rather than lying flat. Part of the reason for this extra complexity, Lamborghini says, is so that the 4.0-liter, twin-turbo V-8 remains a focal point of the car. What’s more, storing the top vertically actually *lowers* the center of gravity by an additional 3mm relative to the closed configuration, all without altering the car’s weight distribution.


Lamborghini


Lamborghini


By approaching the chassis engineering from an open-top-first standpoint, engineers focused on retaining as much structural rigidity as possible even without the roof as a load-bearing element. Relative to the Huracán Spyder, which debuted in 2015, the Temerario Spyder is six percent stiffer in both static and dynamic torsional rigidity.


Lamborghini


Like its[coupe sibling](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/2026-lamborghini-temerario-track-review-worthy-successor/) , the Temerario Spyder utilizes a hybrid powertrain that pairs the aforementioned 4.0-liter, twin-turbo V-8 with three axial flux electric motors and an eight-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission. Total system output is an eye-watering 907 hp. With two electric motors on the front axle and the third between the engine and transmission, performance figures are appropriately stout: Lamborghini claims 2.8 seconds to 62 mph from a standstill, and just 7.3 seconds to clear 124 mph from a dig. Top speed rings in at 213 mph. On our[first drive of the Temerario coupe](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/lamborghini-temerario-review-first-drive/) last year, we lauded the hybrid drivetrain’s seamless operation.


Lamborghini


The engineers took careful measures to optimize the aerodynamic behavior of the Temerario Spyder during drop-top cruising, altering both the upper windscreen crossmember and the rear section of the roof to mitigate turbulent air intruding into the cabin. An adjustable rear window can be lowered or raised to alter how much airflow and engine noise gets into the cabin, as well.


If you want an open-air Lamborghini new from the dealer, the Temerario Spyder is now your only choice. The range-topping[Reveulto](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/lamborghini-revuelto/) is only offered in coupe form, and the[Urus SUV](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/2027-lamborghini-urus-se-performante-specs-pictures/) —well, let’s just say we don’t need another Nissan Murano Crosscab situation.
